title: VISTO: An open-source device to measure exposure time in psychological experiments
author: De Cesarei, Marzocchi, et al.

steps.title: Set up stimulus display parameters
steps.instruction: Configure an ASUS VG245HE LCD monitor to a 60 Hz refresh rate, display uniform black or white patches for durations ranging from 16.67 ms to 150 ms in 16.67 ms increments, synchronize each onset and offset to the start of a vertical refresh cycle, and run the presentation using E‑Prime 2.0.

steps.title: Acquire luminance waveform data
steps.instruction: Install the Arduino IDE, connect an Arduino Mega 2560, select Tools → Board → "Arduino Mega 2560", open the sketch "Profiles.ino" (Supplementary Code A) and upload it; the device should show "PROFILES Ready!". Install CoolTermWin, edit the file baudrates.ini to add the line "1000000", launch CoolTerm and set the baud rate to 1 000 000 (Connection → Options). In CoolTerm choose Connection → Capture → Textfile → Start, specify the file name and path, then press "Connect" to begin logging. Run the stimulus program, making sure each trial begins with a parallel‑port binary code 00000010; VISTO will acquire data at 5000 Hz for 400 ms and forward it via the USB port. After the run, stop capture with Connection → Capture → Textfile → Stop; the resulting CSV file can be opened with any data‑visualization software.

substeps.instruction: Install Arduino IDE and connect Arduino Mega 2560
Select board "Arduino Mega 2560" in Tools → Board
Open and upload sketch "Profiles.ino"; verify "PROFILES Ready!" message
Install CoolTermWin and add "1000000" to baudrates.ini
Launch CoolTerm and set baud rate to 1 000 000
Set capture file name/path via Connection → Capture → Textfile → Start

Run stimulus program with a parallel‑port trigger (binary 00000010) at each trial start
VISTO records at 5000 Hz for 400 ms and sends data to USB
Stop capture with Connection → Capture → Textfile → Stop

steps.title: Calibrate VISTO photodiode thresholds
steps.instruction: Present a black screen then a white screen on the monitor while the photodiode is attached, press the black/white calibration button, and record the minimum and maximum AD values observed over a 100 ms interval (e.g., 6–7 AD for black, 253–255 AD for white). Adjust the variable resistors until the black and white values are as far apart as possible; the range must be at least 50 AD units (giving a minimum threshold of 5 AD). Compute the threshold as 10 % of the black‑to‑white range (e.g., range = 250 − 10 = 240 AD, threshold = 24 AD) and set the black‑to‑white transition point at black_max + threshold (e.g., 10 + 24 = 34 AD).

substeps.instruction: Display a black patch and record the minimum AD value over 100 ms
Display a white patch and record the maximum AD value over 100 ms
Adjust variable resistors to maximize the black‑white separation
Verify that the black‑white range ≥ 50 AD units (threshold ≥ 5 AD)
Calculate threshold = 0.10 × (range) and set transition point at black_max + threshold

steps.title: Measure exposure time with VISTO
steps.instruction: Install the sketch "ExpTime.ino" (Supplementary Code B) on the Arduino Mega 2560; after upload the device displays "EXPTIME Ready!" and no PC connection is required unless you wish to save the results. Run the calibration procedure described above. Then run the experiment consisting of alternating black and white patches (optionally inserting triggers during black screens). After each black‑to‑white and white‑to‑black transition VISTO shows the exposure time and inter‑trial interval on its built‑in screen and streams the same values in text format over USB (data acquired at 2000 Hz, 8‑bit resolution). The streamed data include absolute timestamps for the start and end of black, the start and end of full white, and the trigger onset.

substeps.instruction: Load and upload sketch "ExpTime.ino"; verify "EXPTIME Ready!" message
Perform the calibration steps from the previous section
Run the experiment with alternating black/white patches and optional triggers
Observe exposure time and ITI displayed on VISTO screen after each transition
Capture streamed text data via USB (2000 Hz, 8‑bit) for later analysis
